newsitem.title: UK: China talk spooks UK cash grain market.
newsitem.headline: China talk spooks UK cash grain market.

text.p: Talk of business to China spooked buyers on the UK cash grain markets on Wednesday.
Prices jumped around one stg a tonne following a surge in futures values on talk that 50,000 tonnes of wheat is going to be loaded in March for shipment to China.
However, most traders were sceptical although one exporter confirmed that there was a vessel due to load in Tilbury, could not confirm that it was going to China.
The talk was enough to trigger active trading on the fob market where feed wheat for Mar fetched 97.50 stg while from 99.50 stg upto 100.25 stg and back down to 99.75 stg was paid for May.
June feed wheat fetched 101 stg a tonne fob ex-east coast ports.
"It may only have been a rumour but it was enough to spook some of the buyers," said one broker.
The China talk and higher futures led to some active trading on the delivered market with Norfolk/Suffolk seeing the bulk of the feed wheat business.
Feed wheat in that area traded at 98 and 98.50 stg for March and from 100.50 stg up to 101.50 stg for Apr/Jun.
In West Norfolk Apr traded at 99 stg and Apr/Jun at 100 stg.
"If you have been lucky enough to be working East Anglia you've had a very good day, but the rest of the trade was been very quiet," said a broker.
